#Summary

This report explores the relationship betwen the number of embassies and democracy scores using three different measures of democracy: POLITY2, TOTLIB1, and V2X_LIBDEM. The report contains exploratory data analysis visualizations of the democracy variables and their relationships to the number of embassies. This is followed by results from mixed effects multivariate Poisson regression modeling.  Poisson regression was chosen since the response variable was count data and mixed effects were used to account for correlations withint he same country across years.  For each democracy measure, we considered the democracy measure along with lagged version of the democracy measure for 1, 2, and 3 year lags.  We then fit a reduced and a full model for each combination.  The reduced model contains only democracy score as fixed effect with random effects for year and country.  Full models contained all the predictors as the reduced model in addtion to population (log transformed), GNI (log transformed), trade imports (log transformed), trade exports (log transformed), a cold war indicator, and interaction between cold war and ideology, colonial past, and region.  

Results of the reduced models can be found in Tables 1-3.  In the reduced models, POLITY2 was found to be significant with a coefficient estimate of -0.014 (SE: 0.003).  This means that that for a one unit inscrease in POLITY2, the number of embassies decreased by 0.014 on average on ***a log scale***.  Another way to interpret this is that for a one unit increase in POLITY2, the number of embassies decreased by about 1.39% (i.e. $e^{-0.014}$ = `r exp(-0.014)`. 1 minus this is approximately 0.0139, hence 1.39%). Additionally, lag1 POLITY2 with a coefficient estimate of -.006 (SE: 0.003).  

Results for full models can be found in Tables 4-6.  POLITY2 is once again found to be the only democracy score that is significant after controlling for additional variables.  It was significant at lags of 0, 1, and 2, with coefficient estimated of -.007, -.008, and -.007.  For lag 0, this indicates a 0.698% drop in number of embassises for each unit increase in POLITY2 on average.  Other variables in the full models that show up as significant include population (log transformed), GNI (log transformed), and Italian colonial past.  All regions of Africa (East, South, Central, and West) had significantly lower average numbers of embassies realtive to the North.  Several other variavles show up as as significant, but not univerally across all lags.  

(Note: In a few cases with larger lags, the model including the cold war indicator and the cold war/ideology interaction effect made the model rank deficient and could not be fit.  This shows up, for example, in Table 4 in the three-year lag column which is missing these coefficients because they were not able to be estimated in this model).  

# Model details

## Reduced model

$$Y_{kt} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{kt})$$

$$\text{log}(\lambda_{kt}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{1kt} + \gamma_{0k} + \gamma_{0t} + \epsilon_{kt}$$

$$\gamma_{0k} \sim \text{N}(0, \sigma_k^2)$$

$$\gamma_{0t} \sim \text{N}(0, \sigma_t^2)$$ where $Y_{kt}$ is the number of embassies for country $k$ in year $t$ and $X_{1kt}$ is one of the democracy scores for country $k$ in year $t$. We also considered models where the democracy score as a predictor was lagged by 1, 2, or 3 years (i.e. for a single lag: $\text{log}(\lambda_{kt}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{1k(t-1)} + \gamma_{0k} + \gamma_{0t} + \epsilon_{kt}$ where $X_{1k(t-1)}$ is the democracy score in the prior year.)

## Full model


$$Y_{kt} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{kt})$$

$$\text{log}(\lambda_{kt}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{1kt} + \ldots + \beta_7X_{7kt} + \gamma_{0k} + \gamma_{0t} + \epsilon_{kt}$$

$$\gamma_{0k} \sim \text{N}(0, \sigma_k^2)$$

$$\gamma_{0t} \sim \text{N}(0, \sigma_t^2)$$

where again $Y_{kt}$ is the number of embassies for country $k$ in year $t$ and $X_{1kt}$ is one of the democracy scores for country $k$ in year $t$. The additional $X$'s represent country's GNI (log trasnformed), population (log trasnformed), trade imports (log trasnformed), trade exports (log trasnformed), region, colonization status after World War II, whether the year is during the Cold War, and an interaction between the cold war indicator and ideology. We also considered models where the democracy score as a predictor was lagged by 1, 2, or 3 years (i.e. for a single lag: $\text{log}(\lambda_{kt}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1X_{1k(t-1)} + \gamma_{0k} + \gamma_{0t} + \epsilon_{kt}$ where $X_{1k(t-1)}$ is the democracy score in the prior year.)


```{r message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(here)

#masterset = read_excel("./data/MASTER DATASET - 9.10.2026.xlsx")

masterset = read_csv(here("data", "MASTER DATASET - 9.10.2026.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(toupper)

odagkey = read_csv(here("data","odag_key.csv"), skip = 1) %>% na.omit() %>% mutate(`Variable Name` = str_to_upper(`Variable Name`), `Variable Name` = gsub("[^A-Z0-9]", "", x = `Variable Name`))

## Cleaning data ##

masterset = masterset %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ na_if(., -99)),
         across(where(is.numeric), ~ na_if(., -88)),
         across(where(is.numeric), ~ na_if(., -77)),
         across(where(is.numeric), ~ na_if(., -66)),
         COUNTRY = case_when(COUNTRY == "seychelles" ~ "Seychelles",
                             COUNTRY == "sao tome & Principe" ~ "Sao Tome & Principe",
                             .default = COUNTRY),
         COLD_WAR = ifelse(YEAR >= 1992, 0, 1), 
         COLPAST1 = as.factor(COLPAST1),
         REGION = as.factor(REGION),
         IDEOLOGY = as.factor(IDEOLOGY))

# Convert commas to periods. 
# It looks like commas are being used as the decimal.  
# Fix the nonsense formatting from excel. 

masterset$GNI <- gsub(",",".",masterset$GNI)
masterset$GNI <- gsub(" ","",masterset$GNI)%>% as.numeric()

masterset$GNI_CAP <- gsub(",",".",masterset$GNI_CAP)
masterset$GNI_CAP <- gsub(" ","",masterset$GNI_CAP)%>% as.numeric()

masterset$POPULATN <- gsub(",",".",masterset$POPULATN)
masterset$POPULATN <- gsub(" ","",masterset$POPULATN) %>% as.numeric()

masterset <- masterset %>% 
  mutate(N_EMBASSY = select(., C099:C572) %>% rowSums(na.rm = T))

#Filter out only years with embassy data
keep_years <- masterset %>% 
  group_by(YEAR) %>% 
  summarize(N_EMBASSY = sum(N_EMBASSY)) %>%
  filter(N_EMBASSY > 0) %>% 
  pull(YEAR)

keep_years <- keep_years[keep_years != 2024]

masterset <- masterset %>% filter(YEAR %in% keep_years)


# Manually fixing names
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TRDX352b")] <- "TRDEX352b" # These years are getting dropped.  
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TRDX200h")] <- "TRDEX200h"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TRDX200m")] <- "TRDEX200m"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDX321sr")] <- "TRDEX321sr"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDX321sm")] <- "TRDEX321sm"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDX321yr")] <- "TRDEX321yr"

names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TRDI200h")] <- "TRDIM200h"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TRDI200m")] <- "TRDIM200m"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDI321sr")] <- "TRDIM321sr"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDI321sm")] <- "TRDIM321sm"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDI321yr")] <- "TRDIM321yr"
names(masterset)[which(names(masterset) == "TDI316SU")] <- "TRDIM316su"

masterset <- masterset %>% mutate(ODAG404 = as.numeric(ODAG404))
masterset <- masterset %>% mutate(ODAG600 = as.numeric(ODAG600))

masterset <- masterset %>% 
  mutate(across(c(ODAG600, ODAG601, ODAG609, ODAG610, ODAG613:ODAGARBC, ODAGARBA:ODAGIAEA, ODAGRDBTOT, 
                  ODAGFAO:ODAGWBTOT, ODAGAF:ODAGGGGI), ~ as.numeric(.x))) %>% # Make these variables numeric
  mutate(across(c(ODAG600, ODAG601, ODAG609, ODAG610, ODAG613:ODAGARBC, ODAGARBA:ODAGIAEA, ODAGRDBTOT, 
                  ODAGFAO:ODAGWBTOT, ODAGAF:ODAGGGGI), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) %>% # Replace NA with 0
  mutate(across(c(ODAG600, ODAG601, ODAG609, ODAG610, ODAG613:ODAGARBC, ODAGARBA:ODAGIAEA, ODAGRDBTOT, 
                  ODAGFAO:ODAGWBTOT, ODAGAF:ODAGGGGI), ~ pmax(.x, 0))) %>% # No negative numbers
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(ODAGTOT200_501 = rowSums(across(ODAG201:ODAG501))) %>% 
  mutate(HHI = rowSums((across(ODAG201:ODAG501) / rowSums(across(ODAG201:ODAG501)))^2)) %>% 
  mutate(HHI = ifelse(ODAGTOT200_501 == 0, NA, HHI))

odag_countries = odagkey %>%
  filter(Classification == "Countries") %>%
  pull(`Variable Name`)

odag_io = odagkey %>%
  filter(Classification == "IOs") %>%
  mutate(`Variable Name` = case_when(`Variable Name` == "ODAG615" ~ "ODAG615 IMF", .default = `Variable Name`)) %>%
  pull(`Variable Name`)

odag_total = odagkey %>%
  filter(Classification == "Total") %>%
  pull(`Variable Name`)

masterset = masterset %>%
  mutate(ODAG_COUNTRIES = rowSums(across(all_of(odag_countries)), na.rm = T),
         ODAG_IO = rowSums(across(all_of(odag_io)), na.rm = T),
         ODAG_TOT = ODAG_COUNTRIES + ODAG_IO)

# HHI values over time

# HHI %>% select(COUNTRY, YEAR, HHI, ODAGTOT200_500, ODAG201:ODAG416) %>% write.csv(file = "./HHI.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#HHI %>% ggplot(aes(x = YEAR, y = HHI)) + geom_line() +  facet_wrap(~COUNTRY) + theme_bw()

## Prepare data for analysis

masterset <- masterset %>% mutate(across(TRDEX351:TRDEX203, ~ as.numeric(.x))) %>% 
  mutate(across(TRDIM351:TRDIM203, ~ as.numeric(.x))) %>% 
  mutate(TRDEXTOT = rowSums(pick(TRDEX351:TRDEX250, 
                                 TRDEX300:TRDEX285, 
                                 TRDEX280:TRDEX415,
                                 TRDEX100:TRDEX147,
                                 TRDEX577:TRDEX551,
                                 TRDEX563:TRDEX203),na.rm = TRUE),
         TRDIMTOT = rowSums(pick(TRDIM351:TRDIM250,
                                 TRDIM300:TRDIM285,
                                 TRDIM280:TRDIM415,
                                 TRDIM100:TRDIM147,
                                 TRDIM577:TRDIM551,
                                 TRDIM563:TRDIM203),na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  mutate(ODAGTOT = rowSums(pick(ODAG201:ODAG501), na.rm = T),
         ODAGTOT_private = rowSums(pick(c(ODAG600, ODAG601, ODAG609, ODAG610, ODAG613:ODAGARBC, ODAGARBA:ODAGIAEA, ODAGRDBTOT, 
                                          ODAGFAO:ODAGWBTOT, ODAGAF:ODAGGGGI)), na.rm = T)) %>% 
  filter(ODAGTOT_private >= 0,
         ODAG_IO >= 0,
         ODAG_COUNTRIES >= 0,
         ODAG_TOT >= 0) %>%
  mutate(POPULATN = ifelse(POPULATN == -99, NA, POPULATN),
         logGNI = log(GNI, 10),
         logPOP = log(POPULATN,10),
         logTRDIMtot = log(TRDIMTOT + 1,10),
         logTRDEXtot = log(TRDEXTOT + 1,10), 
         logODAGtot = log(ODAGTOT + 1, 10)) 

# Now create the lag variables

masterset <- masterset %>% arrange(CCODE, YEAR) %>% group_by(CCODE) %>% 
  mutate(TOTLIB1_lag1 = lag(TOTLIB1,1),
         TOTLIB1_lag2 = lag(TOTLIB1,2),
         TOTLIB1_lag3 = lag(TOTLIB1,3),
         POLITY_lag1 = lag(POLITY,1),
         POLITY_lag2 = lag(POLITY,2),
         POLITY_lag3 = lag(POLITY,3),
         POLITY2_lag1 = lag(POLITY2,1),
         POLITY2_lag2 = lag(POLITY2,2),
         POLITY2_lag3 = lag(POLITY2,3),
         V2X_LIBDEM_lag1 = lag(V2X_LIBDEM,1),
         V2X_LIBDEM_lag2 = lag(V2X_LIBDEM,2),
         V2X_LIBDEM_lag3 = lag(V2X_LIBDEM,3)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() 
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

Below are the distributions of the three democracy variables.

```{r}
masterset %>% filter(!is.na(POLITY2)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = factor(POLITY2))) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~YEAR) + theme_bw() + xlab("POLITY2")
masterset %>% filter(!is.na(TOTLIB1)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = factor(TOTLIB1))) + geom_bar() + facet_wrap(~YEAR) + theme_bw() + xlab("TOTLIB1") + scale_x_discrete(breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 11, 14, NA))
masterset %>% filter(!is.na(V2X_LIBDEM)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = factor(YEAR), y = V2X_LIBDEM)) + geom_boxplot() +theme_bw() + xlab("v2x_LIBDEM")
```

The plot below is the number of embassies over time with each connected line representing a single country.

```{r}
masterset %>% ggplot(aes(x = YEAR, y = N_EMBASSY, group = COUNTRY)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + theme_bw() 
```

Next, scatter plots of the number of the democracy variables versus the embassies are plotted and each plot includes a trend line of the relationship.

Below are the summaries for the full models for ODAG from external countries. As with the reduced model summaries, the $\hat{\beta}$ coefficients are starred by significance as denoted in each table, with their respective standard error below.

```{r}
## FULL MODEL SUMMARIES

mod1_summary_V2X_LIBDEM <- modelsummary(
  models = list(
    "Unlagged" = mod1_V2X_LIBDEM,
```
